name: Branchial Cleft Anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiologic Diagnosis of Branchial Cleft Anomalies

criteria.description: Presence of cysts, sinuses, or fistulas located along the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle
Imaging studies (ultrasound, CT, or MRI) demonstrating cystic or tract lesions consistent with branchial cleft origin
Congenital or early childhood onset of neck mass or drainage
Histopathological confirmation showing squamous epithelial lining with lymphoid tissue in cyst wall

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a cyst, sinus, or fistula along the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle with supportive imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; histopathology is confirmatory post-excision.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Lateral neck cyst along anterior sternocleidomastoid
searchTerms: neck cyst on front side of neck muscle

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent sinus tract opening on lateral neck
searchTerms: persistent open sinus on side of neck

common.symptomName: Intermittent mucopurulent discharge from sinus or fistula
searchTerms: intermittent pus discharge from neck sinus

common.symptomName: Recurrent neck infections or abscess formation
Tenderness over cyst or sinus tract during infection
searchTerms: tenderness on neck cyst when infected
difficulty swallowing due to neck mass

occasional.symptomName: Erythema and swelling of overlying skin
searchTerms: redness and swelling of skin over cyst
limited neck movement due to swelling
airway blockage from large neck cyst

rare.symptomName: Malignant transformation (e.g., carcinoma arising in cyst)

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers during infection (e.g., ESR, CRP)
Normal routine blood counts unless infected
imaging: Ultrasound showing anechoic or hypoechoic cystic lesion
CT or MRI demonstrating cyst or fistulous tract along anterior border of sternocleidomastoid
Contrast studies may delineate fistula tract
other: Histopathology showing cyst lined by squamous epithelium with lymphoid aggregates
Clinical history of congenital neck mass or sinus

distinguishingFeatures: Moves with swallowing or tongue protrusion
No persistent sinus or fistula tract

redFlags: Recurrent severe infections or abscess formation
references: Nayak DR, et al. Branchial cleft anomalies: a review of 52 cases. Indian J Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 2015.
